S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major changes in working hours or conditions
patient_info.stressor: When Charles Hoff’s cleaning contract shifted from predictable early-morning building rounds to a rotating schedule with evening events, urgent room turnovers, and more direct contact with church groups, tenants, and new staff, the structure that had helped him compensate for his lifelong high energy became much thinner. Over the next 1 year and 5 months, coworkers increasingly experienced him as unable to slow down during meetings, too quick to answer before instructions were finished, and impatient when supply-room decisions or elevator access required waiting. His restlessness and constant motion began interfering with staff training, inventory checks, and occupant complaints, creating enough workplace friction that his supervisor recommended the employee assistance program. Charles agreed to psychiatric evaluation after his wife also noticed that even fishing trips, bingo nights, and woodworking had become hard for him to approach calmly or quietly.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: What brings me in is I feel like I’ve got a motor humming under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still, like in staff meetings or church event briefings, and I end up shifting, standing, or finding some excuse to move around.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even when I’m trying to relax, like fishing with my wife or sitting through bingo, I catch myself tapping, talking too loud, messing with my tackle box or pencil, and it gets hard for me to just be quiet and enjoy it.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: On my shifts I go from mopping to checking trash to straightening chairs without really stopping, and even at home I’ll start puttering in the garage or re-sorting tools instead of sitting down after work.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: When my supervisor or one of the church staff starts giving me instructions, I jump in with what I think they’re going to say before they finish, and sometimes I get it wrong and have to be corrected.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Waiting for the freight elevator, the supply closet key, or somebody else to decide what room needs cleaning next makes me antsy and short, and I’ll pace or push to get moving before it’s really my turn.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I remember getting in trouble back in grade school for popping out of my seat, talking over the teacher, and rushing ahead before directions were finished; my mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight even as a kid.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: At work it has started causing complaints and corrections because I miss parts of instructions and create friction during room turnovers and supply decisions, to the point my supervisor pushed me toward the employee assistance program.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This worse stretch has been going on for about a year and five months, ever since my cleaning contract changed to rotating hours and more event work.
